discrepancies.title: OM 'net' yield 6.8% vs buyer's net 4.7%
discrepancies.why: The OM calls the yield net, but the 'net' yield equals the gross yield on asking price (6.9%); and it deducts AED 150,000 of costs from AED 11,210,000, against AED 2,869,767 of Year-1 operating costs a buyer bears. The screen uses Year-1 NOI after the mandate's vacancy, collection loss, management fee, full opex and input VAT.

impact.basis: engine Year-1 NOI minus the net income the OM yield implies

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker for the costs behind the net yield; rebuild NOI from the operating statement and service-charge budget.

discrepancies.title: 66.7% of in-place rent is from units let above market

sources.label: 63 let units above the area reference rent

discrepancies.why: In a falling 2026 market these leases are AED 585,995 a year above reference rent; the engine resets each to market at expiry. The mandate limit is 20.0%.

impact.basis: engine Year-1 NOI with the 63 over-rented leases at market reference rent today, minus the base case (which resets them only at expiry)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Check the over-rented leases' expiry dates and tenants; price the reset into the offer.

discrepancies.title: Operating statement omits district cooling
discrepancies.why: The building is chiller-free, so the landlord pays district cooling, yet the statement has no cooling line. A whole-building owner bears these costs; the screen fills each from the mandate default per sq ft of NSA (the management fee is always the mandate's % of EGI).

impact.basis: engine Year-1 NOI if the absent costs were zero, as the statement implies, minus the base case with mandate defaults; the delta is how much the statement overstates NOI

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the missing bills (Empower/chiller, insurance schedule, reserve study, management agreement).

discrepancies.title: OM yield 6.8% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 10,100,382 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 4.7%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Pass.** The deal fails a hard filter first: Year-1 DSCR is 1.20x [[uw.dscr_year1]], below the 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] floor. It also misses several soft tests: going-in net yield on total cost of 4.73% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] against a 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum; levered IRR of -6.73% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] against 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]]; equity multiple of 0.71x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] against 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]]; and 66.66% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of income let above market against a 20.00% [[mandate.max_over_rent_share_of_income.threshold]] limit.

Recommendation: do not commit diligence spend at the asking price of AED 162.50m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. Re-engage only near our walk-away price of AED 113.91m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], which is 29.90% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] below asking and is set by the levered IRR target.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Kestrel Tower, Business Bay, completed 2019 [[deal.completion_year]], 107 units [[rr.unit_count]], freehold single title.
- **Price:** AED 162.50m [[uw.price_aed]], or AED 1,835 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. On BUA it is AED 1,137 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]].
- **Income:** Direct leases, no master tenant. In-place rent is AED 11.21m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. Occupancy is 93.46% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units and 91.66% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area, with 7 [[rr.vacant_units]] units vacant (rent roll dated 31 October 2026 [[rr.as_of]]).

The OM headlines a 6.81% [[om.yield_stated]] net yield on asking price. On a buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 4.73% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. On price alone it is 5.02% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_price]].

## What would make it fail
1. **Thin debt cover.** DSCR is already under the floor. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower it falls to 1.16x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.dscr_year1]]. Year-1 NOI only just covers debt service at 82.77% [[uw.breakeven_occupancy_dscr_1]] occupancy.
2. **No exit rescues it.** The base exit value is AED 130.86m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], well below the price we would pay. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, levered IRR is still -1.45% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, it is -12.49% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
3. **Over-renting meets expiries.** Two-thirds of rent comes from leases above market, and the base case assumes market rent falls 4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1. The largest expiry window runs from 31 July 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] to 30 October 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. It holds 30.39% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent, or AED 3.41m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]]. That is inside the 40.00% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]] limit, but those leases reset toward market.
4. **Costs are understated in the operating statement.** The statement shows NOI of AED 9.69m [[opex.noi_aed]] and an expense ratio of 15.42% [[opex.opex_ratio]]. The screen's ratio is 26.01% [[uw.opex_ratio_year1]].

## Discrepancies that matter
- **High: the OM's "net" yield is not net.** It equals the gross yield on asking price, 6.9% [[disc.gross_yield_as_net.why]]. It deducts only AED 150,000 [[disc.gross_yield_as_net.why]] of costs from AED 11,210,000 [[disc.gross_yield_as_net.why]]. The screen relied on its own Year-1 NOI, after vacancy, collection loss, management fee, full opex and input VAT, with operating costs of AED 2,869,767 [[disc.gross_yield_as_net.why]]. Its Year-1 NOI sits AED -2.90m [[disc.gross_yield_as_net.impact_delta_aed]] against the net income the OM yield implies.
- **High: over-rented leases.** These leases sit AED 585,995 [[disc.over_rented_vs_market.why]] a year above reference rent in a falling market. The screen resets each to market at expiry. Resetting all of them today would cut Year-1 NOI by a further AED -167k [[disc.over_rented_vs_market.impact_delta_aed]].
- **High: no district cooling in the statement.** The landlord pays cooling, yet the statement has no line for it. The screen used a mandate default of AED 797k [[uw.opex_default.district_cooling]], not an actual bill. That is how much the statement overstates NOI.

The medium item (yield before acquisition costs) is covered in the returns section above. Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- Broker's breakdown of the costs behind the OM's net yield.
- Operating statement and service-charge budget, to rebuild NOI.
- Over-rented leases: expiry dates and tenants.
- Actual district cooling (chiller) bills.
- Insurance schedule, reserve study and management agreement.
- The OM's basis for its stated annual rent, which it leaves unstated.
